subject: Shut the guest down before a quit turns the VM off
message:
Shut the guest down before a quit turns the VM off

Closing the VM window, ⌘Q, `vm stop` and Control-C used to end the
virtual machine at once, as pulling the power would. vphone-vm now asks
vphoned for `system.shutdown` first and exits when the guest stops. A
guest still running after 15 seconds, or one that refuses, is turned
off; `vm stop` sends SIGKILL after 20 seconds, so the wait stays below
it. A guest that cannot be asked (DFU, still starting up, or a vphoned
without `system_shutdown`) is turned off at once, as before.

The window and ⌘Q still ask first, with text that says which of the two
will happen. A SIGINT that arrives while the question is up answers it,
and a second SIGINT while the guest shuts down turns it off without
waiting.

Tested on a fresh iPad 27.0.1 machine: a SIGINT, a quit confirmed with
Stop, and a quit answered by SIGINT each ended in "Guest stopped" within
5 seconds.

subject: Tell a running machine from a stopped one before touching its state
message:
Tell a running machine from a stopped one before touching its state

Cloning, snapshotting and reverting copy or replace a machine's disk
image, SEPStorage and nvram.bin. A running vphone-vm keeps all three
open and they advance together (the SEP's anti-replay counters and the
xART gigalocker on the disk), so a copy taken while it runs can pair a
disk with SEP state from another moment, and that guest panics in the
SEP on its next boot.

VPhoneBundleActivity looks for any process of this user holding one of
the three open, matched by device and inode, and treats a control
socket that accepts a connection as running too, which covers a VM
started under sudo that cannot be inspected without root.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Save and revert a stopped machine's disk state with vm snapshot
message:
Save and revert a stopped machine's disk state with vm snapshot

A snapshot is <machine>/Snapshots/<name>/: APFS clones of the disk
image, SEPStorage and nvram.bin from one moment, plus PatchReceipt.plist
and restore-info.json when present, and a Snapshot.plist with the name,
creation date, note and which state files were present or absent. The
three storage files advance as a pair with the SEP's anti-replay state,
so create and revert both require the machine to be stopped
(VPhoneBundleActivity.requireStopped) and always move all of them.

The receipt and restore-info.json describe the guest (live patches, the
restored OS, whether cfw install finished), so they follow the disk; one
that was absent at snapshot time is removed on revert. config.plist
(identity and settings), patch choices, the restore tree, originals,
ROMs and Launchpad's launchpad.json stay as they are. Files a client
adds to a snapshot folder are kept and deleted with the snapshot.

Create builds the snapshot in a hidden staging folder and renames it
into place exclusively. Revert clones every file into a staging folder
in the machine first and only then renames each over the live one.
Off APFS clonefile fails and the operation is refused rather than
copying a disk image. vm export leaves Snapshots/ out.

CLI: vm snapshot create <vm> <name> [--note], list <vm> [--json],
revert <vm> <name> [--force], delete <vm> <name> [--force]. list --json
prints [{"name","created","note"}], oldest first, ISO 8601 dates, note
omitted when empty. vm info shows the snapshot count when there is one.

Tests: VPhoneCoreKitTests (389, including the new BundleSnapshotsTests)
and VPhoneArchiveKitTests (65, including export leaving snapshots
behind) pass; VPhoneCommand builds; the CLI was exercised against a
throwaway library.

Live on an iOS 27.0 guest cloned from a stopped machine: snapshot
"base" of the stopped clone, a marker file written in the guest, then
vm snapshot revert --force; after the next boot the marker was gone,
vphoned answered, and the UDID, Wi-Fi MAC and IP were unchanged. A
declined revert prompt changed nothing (same inodes and checksums), and
create and revert were refused while the machine ran. A snapshot shared
all but 0.16 GB of its disk blocks with the reverted, rebooted machine.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Give a cloned machine its own device identity on request
message:
Give a cloned machine its own device identity on request

A plain vm clone keeps the machine identifier (the ECID) and the MAC
address, so the copy is a backup that cannot run beside its source, and
the help told users to edit the identity themselves without saying what
is safe to change. Only the ECID is: SEPStorage, the xART gigalocker and
the Data and User volume keys were made together by one restore, and a
replaced SEPStorage panics the SEP at boot.

vm clone --new-identity clears machineIdentifier and the MAC in the
copy's config.plist, so vphone-vm generates new ones on the first start,
and the guest derives a new UDID from the new ECID. It also clears the
fixed IPv4 address, port forwards and a hand-chosen mDNS name, which
would collide with the source's; an mDNS name that `--mdns on` derived
from the machine name follows the new name, as it does on rename. It
also deletes udid-prediction.txt. nvram.bin,
SEPStorage and the disk image stay as copied: the boot chain's patched
image4 property callback already ignores the ECID in the old tickets,
so no re-personalization is needed. The command prints which network
settings it cleared.

Every clone now refuses while the source runs, so the disk image and
SEPStorage are copied from one moment, rolls back a half-made copy on
failure, and leaves out the source's stale vphone.sock and its
Snapshots directory.

Research/Host/machine_identity_and_clone.md records where identity
lives, the SEPStorage replacement tests and the measured disk cost
(about 0.35 GB per clone after its first boots on APFS).

Tested with the VPhoneCoreKitTests scheme (394 tests; new ones cover
the new identity, a derived mDNS name, a plain clone's leftovers,
refusal while a state file is held open, and the cleared-settings list)
and a VPhoneCommand build.

Live on iOS 27.0: a stopped machine was cloned plainly to a golden copy
that was never booted, and two --new-identity clones of it were started
together. Each came up with its own ECID, UDID (lockdown agreed), MAC
and DHCP address, the guest asked to trust the Mac again, and each held
0.33-0.52 GB of its own after booting, the other 19.6 GB shared with the
golden copy. Clones of a running machine were refused.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Clone with a new identity and keep disk snapshots in Launchpad

it runs beside the original, and the guest asks to trust the Mac again on
its first connection. Turned off, it is the plain copy it was before.

A machine's menu gains Snapshots…, a sheet listing `vm snapshot list

Delete…. Revert and delete ask first; revert says the current disk, SEP
storage and NVRAM are lost unless snapshotted. The list can be read while
the machine runs, the actions wait for it to stop, and the sheet shows
the command under way and its own errors.

A snapshot does not include launchpad.json, but the guest environment and
boot chain it records live on the disk and NVRAM a revert replaces. So
after taking one Launchpad saves the binding to
Snapshots/<name>/launchpad.json (same checks as the machine's own, never
through a link), and after a revert takes bootChain and guestEnvironment
from it while keeping the bundle chosen now.

The argument builders, the list decoder and the binding round trip are
plain functions covered by Tests/MachineSnapshotsTests.sh. The DEBUG
snapshot driver renders the clone sheet, the Snapshots sheet (stopped,
running, empty) and Take Snapshot with mock data.

bundle.

subject: Count a control socket that refuses this user as a running VM
message:
Count a control socket that refuses this user as a running VM

VPhoneBundleActivity counted only a successful connect to vphone.sock as
running. A VM started under sudo runs as root: libproc refuses to list
its file descriptors (EPERM), so the scan for the disk image, SEPStorage
and nvram.bin skips it, and its vphone.sock is root-owned with mode 0755,
so this user's connect fails with EACCES. Both checks then said stopped,
and vm clone, vm snapshot create and vm snapshot revert copied or
replaced the state files of a running guest, which panics the SEP on its
next boot. The doc comment already claimed the socket probe covered the
sudo case; it did not.

Only two outcomes now mean stopped: no socket at the path (nothing
there, or something that is not a socket, judged by lstat without
following a link), and a connect that fails with ECONNREFUSED or ENOENT,
which is what the socket file of an exited VM returns. Every other
failure means a socket exists that something may be serving, and
refusing a clone is cheap while copying a live guest is not, so it
counts as running. A path too long for sun_path cannot be probed and
counts as running for the same reason; removing a stale socket by hand
clears it.

New tests: a listening socket chmod'ed to 0 (connect fails with EACCES
even for its owner) is running, and a plain file at vphone.sock is not;
the existing test still shows a stale socket passes as stopped.
VPhoneCoreKitTests (396) pass. One earlier run failed LaunchLayoutTests
"finds a running vphone-vm by its config", which waits 0.2 s for a child
process and is unrelated; it passed on the rerun.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Make snapshot revert all or nothing and trust its metadata less
message:
Make snapshot revert all or nothing and trust its metadata less

Three holes in machine disk snapshots, each of which could leave a disk
image with a SEPStorage or NVRAM from another moment, which panics the
guest's SEP at boot:

- Revert took the Files and AbsentFiles lists of Snapshot.plist on
  trust, checking only that each was a plain name other than
  config.plist. An edited or damaged plist could list the disk image
  alone, so revert paired it with the live SEPStorage, or name
  Disk.img or launchpad.json as absent, so revert deleted it. Revert
  now refuses the snapshot as damaged before touching anything unless
  Files holds every state file (disk image, SEPStorage, nvram.bin),
  both lists name only state files and optional state files, and no
  file is listed twice or in both.
- The swap renamed each staged copy over its live file in turn, so a
  rename failing halfway left a mix and said nothing about it. Each
  live file is now moved aside into the staging directory before its
  snapshot copy takes its place, an absent file is moved aside rather
  than unlinked, and a failure moves everything back in reverse. The
  old files go only with the staging directory once every step has
  succeeded. If putting them back fails too, the new revertIncomplete
  error names the files and says the state may be inconsistent and to
  revert again before starting the VM.
- Create checked that the VM was stopped only before cloning. It now
  checks again after the clones, before the rename that publishes the
  snapshot, as revert does before its swap; a refusal removes the
  staging directory as any other failure does.

The snapshots guide says a revert is all or nothing and that a
snapshot listing the wrong files is refused.

New tests: revert refuses ten edited file lists (missing a required
file, a non-state file in either list, a path, overlaps, repeats) and
leaves every live file byte for byte as it was; with nvram.bin or the
absent restore-info.json made immutable, a revert fails partway, puts
every live file back, leaves no staging directory, and goes through
once the flag is cleared. The create re-check has no deterministic
test: it would need a seam to start a VM between the clones and the
rename, and the existing held-open test covers the refusal itself.

VPhoneCoreKitTests: 396 tests pass (one run first hit a timing failure
in LaunchLayoutTests' running vphone-vm stand-in, unrelated; two reruns
passed).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Check again after a clone's copy that the source is still stopped
message:
Check again after a clone's copy that the source is still stopped

started while the copy ran, which off APFS copies entry by entry and can
take minutes, could leave the clone with a disk image and a SEPStorage
or nvram.bin from different moments, and the clone then panics in the

the half-made copy is rolled back as on any other failure and the
running error is thrown. The first check stays, so a running source is
refused before any copying starts.

subject: Let Xcode's DeviceHub show a guest's screen
message:
Let Xcode's DeviceHub show a guest's screen

DeviceHub (Xcode 27) spun forever on every vphone guest. On iOS 27 the
developer disk image never mounted: cryptexd stages each cryptex asset
with fcntl(F_SETPROTECTIONCLASS) and accepts only ENOTSUP as a failure,
and a guest answers EPERM. On a guest with the image mounted, the DDI's
dtremotedisplayd reported no media stream features, because
CoreDeviceUtilities refuses customer devices before 27.0 and every iPad.

libdevicehubfix.dylib is inserted into cryptexd and dtremotedisplayd. It
reports that EPERM as ENOTSUP, and answers the feature getter with what
a Mac host offers (0x8c) and isCustomerRestricted with false.

Validated on iPad16,1 26.6.2: the view shows the live screen. On
iPhone17,3 27.0.1 the image now mounts and the stream starts, but the
view stays black; the capture display fails in backboardd's swap path,
recorded as open in Research/Guest/devicehub_screen_viewing.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Show DeviceHub's capture display on iOS 27 guests
message:
Show DeviceHub's capture display on iOS 27 guests

The iOS 27 force-kern patch sent every IOMobileFramebuffer present to the
kernel userclient, including the capture display DeviceHub's stream adds.
That display has no userclient port, so backboardd's swaps failed with
MACH_SEND_INVALID_DEST and the stream stayed black. Each public swap
trampoline now branches to _kern_Swap* when the connection has a kernel
port and to _virt_Swap* when it does not; the paravirtual main display
keeps presenting through the kernel. ARM64Encoder gains CBZ/CBNZ for it.

The virtual board reports phone11 chrome with no FramebufferIdentifier,
so DeviceHub drew the screen over the bezel corners. libdevicehubfix now
also loads into the DDI's dtdeviceinfod and fills only that missing
answer with Xcode's matching phone11 mask.

Stream latency that grows over a long session is still open; see
Research/Guest/devicehub_screen_viewing.md.

subject: Run CFW installs and updates on different machines side by side
message:
Run CFW installs and updates on different machines side by side

Launchpad allowed one `cfw install`, `cfw update-environment` or `cfw
update-kernel` on the whole Mac at a time. The app streamed every
operation's output through one receiver, and the helper kept one running
process for every connection and user. Updating one machine refused a
second machine's install or update, and with it the `cfw install` step
of creating a machine.

That lock protected nothing the machines share. Each run makes its own
mkdtemp work folder, attaches its own APFS clone of Disk.img, mounts the
guest volumes inside that folder, and refuses to start while anything
else has the machine's Disk.img open. Two runs on different machines
share only free space: each checks for 50 GiB on its own, so two could
pass and then fill the disk together.

- The helper allows one operation per machine, keyed by the machine
  folder's device and inode, so same-named machines in two libraries are
  different machines. It checks a request and registers it under one
  lock. On a volume that running operations already write to, it admits
  another only while there are 50 GiB free for each of them and the new
  one. A volume no other run uses is left to vphone-cli's own check.
- Cancel names the machine. The helper stops only that machine's
  operation, only for the user who started it, and only once its process
  is running.
- The app runs each operation on its own XPC connection. The helper
  sends output only over the connection that made the request, so each
  machine's lines reach its own console log. A second operation on the
  same machine is refused before the authorization prompt.
- The admission rules live in VPhoneLaunchpadHelperFirmwareAdmission,
  tested by VPhoneLaunchpad/Tests/FirmwareAdmissionTests.sh.

The helper protocol changed, so the helper is build 15.

subject: Pin the guest's device name to the one the host writes to NVRAM
message:
Pin the guest's device name to the one the host writes to NVRAM

libdevicename reads NVRAM variable vphone-device-name from
IODeviceTree:/options. When it holds a name, configd publishes that
name as Setup:/System's ComputerName, which lockdownd, MobileGestalt and
UIDevice all read, and lockdownd refuses to rename the device to
anything else. Without the variable every interpose passes through.

configd's preferences monitor publishes the flattened preferences with
one SCDynamicStoreSetMultiple. That call is rewritten rather than the
SCPreferencesGetValue that feeds it, because the monitor's model-change
path writes the value it reads back to preferences.plist. When the call
leaves Setup:/System out as unchanged, the store's value is pinned; when
it removes it, the pinned name is set instead. preferences.plist keeps
the guest's own name.

In lockdownd, SCPreferencesSetComputerName with another name returns
false with kSCStatusAccessError, and the host name setters that follow
on the same preferences object are refused too. A rename to the pinned
name goes through.

The decisions are pure CoreFoundation in DeviceNamePolicy.c and
`make test-devicename` checks them on the host.

subject: Make host location sync a machine setting that actually reaches the guest
message:
Make host location sync a machine setting that actually reaches the guest

Sync Host Location sent nothing that stayed in the guest. Every VM log
that recorded it had VPhoneLocation.app authorized and forwarding fixes,
and every location.set refused with "Location Services are turned off";
vphone-vm only printed that, and the menu checkmark stayed on. Headless
launches started sync unconditionally.

config.plist gains syncsHostLocation (absent means off). It is set with
`vphone-cli vm config <name> --sync-host-location on|off`, shown by
`vm info` and in `vm list --json`, toggled at Location > Sync Host
Location in the VM window (written to config.plist at once; a preset or
a replay pauses sync for that run only), and in a new Location section
of a machine's Settings in Launchpad. A headless launch now syncs only
when the machine is set to.

The guest's Location Services switch is turned on by Setup Assistant's
Location Services pane, so a guest that skipped it has the switch off
and locationd gives no client a location. vphoned leaves the switch to
the guest's Settings: location.set and location.current fail with the
code location_services_off. The VM window says so once, and vphone-vm
offers the last Mac fix again every 10 s, since the Mac sends a new one
only when it moves.

The Mac's locationd stores the code requirement VPhoneLocation.app first
registered with, an ad hoc signature's cdhash, and silently turns away a
helper from another build while one with the stored requirement runs:
it never gets an authorization status. Two machines on different
bundles could not both sync, and a new build's helper got nothing while
an old one ran. StageBundle.sh now signs the helper with
`designated => identifier "com.vphone.bundle.location"`, and
ValidateBundle.sh checks it. That lends nothing new: the helper already
hands the location to whatever starts it.

Launchpad now passes a new vm config option, so the series moves to 2.8:
VPhone.bundle and Launchpad are 2.8.0 and Launchpad requires a 2.8.0
bundle.

Tested on a new iPhone17,3 guest (iOS 27.0, 24A435, standard), in a
window: with the setting off no helper started; with it on, the guest
refused with location_services_off, the window showed the localized
sheet once, and the resend ran every 10 s. Turning Location Services on
in the guest's Settings brought the Mac's coordinate in 6 s later
(fresh, simulated) with the Mac standing still, the resend stopped, and
Maps drew its blue dot there. locationd accepted the identifier
requirement once no cdhash-signed helper ran and authorized the helper
without a prompt. The menu toggle was not exercised live. A headless
guest's locationd deadlocks within a second of starting, with or

subject: Restart a locationd that deadlocked as it started
message:
Restart a locationd that deadlocked as it started

On an iOS 27.0 guest, locationd can deadlock about a second after it
starts. Its main thread runs a run-loop callback
(CLLocationController::sendTechStatusNotification) that syncs into the
controller's silo while that silo's dispatch_once constructor is still
running, and the constructor's next sync into a cohort-0 silo needs the
main queue. Nothing in locationd runs again, and every CoreLocation
client blocks on com.apple.locationd.synchronous for good: location.*
time out after 120 s, and Maps, navd and nearbyd hang with them. Boots
of an unmodified guest hung 6 times in 15 headless and once in 5
windowed, so it is not a headless problem.

Rewriting the two main-thread callbacks to async only moved the hang to
a silo timer, so there is no binary patch. vphoned now starts
GuestLocationdWatchdog: it asks CLLocationManager whether Location
Services are on, every 15 s for the first 5 minutes and every 60 s
after, and when no answer comes in 10 s it SIGKILLs locationd and asks
again a second later, so launchd starts a fresh one. A restart that
deadlocks too is caught the same way, at most 20 times.

Measured on one VM switched between bundles with and without the
watchdog: locationd answered after boot 3 of 5 times without it and 14
of 14 with it; restarted instances answered 3 of 6 times without it and
6 of 6 with it. Details in Research/Guest/locationd_startup_deadlock.md.

subject: Keep a banded stream from deadlocking the host GPU
message:
Keep a banded stream from deadlocking the host GPU

A stream that splits each frame into four bands makes avconferenced read
every captured frame on the GPU once per band, in VideoProcessing's
VCPSideCarMetal. The paravirtual scaler that writes the frame registers
its write on the host 0.25-0.8 ms after taking the request, and a band
read can register first. A command buffer registers the frame's two
planes one at a time, and the host queues new readers behind a waiting
writer, so a write that lands between the two registrations waits for a
read that waits for it. The scaler and the GPU stop, the host restarts
the GPU, and the guest loses it until the VM restarts.

libdevicehubfix now also loads into avconferenced. Before the first band
read of each frame it waits for one synchronous scaler transform between
two scratch surfaces, which the host runs after the frame's write. That
adds 0.76 ms median latency to a frame of a banded stream; a single-band
stream does not reach the replaced methods.

subject: Download IPSWs over several connections at once
message:
Download IPSWs over several connections at once

Apple's CDN holds each connection well below a fast link, so a 12 GB IPSW
took most of an hour over the one GET fw prepare used. Measured against
updates.cdn-apple.com for 15 seconds: one connection 18.9 MB/s, four
45.8 MB/s, eight 28 MB/s.

- VPhoneIPSWCache probes with `Range: bytes=0-0` and reads the size and
  ETag from the 206. Apple's CDN answers ranges but sends no Accept-Ranges,
  so a HEAD would not find it.
- When the server answers ranges, the file downloads as 32 MB segments over
  `connections` workers (default 4), each with its own URLSession: one
  session sends every request over a single HTTP/2 connection. Each segment
  is written in place with pwrite into the .partial file.
- A dropped or short segment resumes from its last written byte; five
  attempts in a row without progress fail it. Segment requests time out
  after a minute idle instead of three hours.
- If-Range carries the probe's ETag, so a file replaced on the server
  midway fails with changedDuringDownload instead of mixing bytes.
- One connection, or a server that ignores ranges, downloads as one GET as
  before. Progress adds up across connections and is reported serially, so
  the bar and Launchpad's `progress` lines are unchanged.
- `fw prepare --download-connections <1-16>` sets the count.

Launchpad passes no new argument, so no minimum-bundle bump.

message:
Read the cfw work folder name while mkdtemp's buffer is alive

makeWorkDirectory passed `&template` to mkdtemp and then read the
returned pointer. That pointer points into the buffer Swift lends for
the call, which is only valid until the call returns, and the array is
not used afterwards, so an optimized build can free it before
String(cString:) reads it. The pin then sees a garbage path, and
`cfw install` and `cfw update-kernel` fail on the work folder.

there.

subject: Share identical disk blocks between machines with vm rebase
message:
Share identical disk blocks between machines with vm rebase

Two machines restored separately from one IPSW share nothing on disk,
yet about 8.6 GB of their ~20 GB of data is byte-identical at the same
offset, mostly the ASR-restored system volume. macOS has no public call
to clone a range of one file into another, but a whole file can be
cloned: `vm rebase <vm> --onto <base>` clones the base's disk image into
a staging file in the machine folder, writes in only the units where
<vm>'s image differs, and renames the result over <vm>'s Disk.img. The
new image holds exactly <vm>'s bytes and keeps the base's blocks
wherever they matched.

- Both machines must be stopped (VPhoneBundleActivity.requireStopped),
  checked before starting and again before the swap, after every
  descriptor is closed; an image whose inode, size, mtime or ctime moved
  in between is not replaced. A machine cannot be its own base, also
  under a second name.
- Only the disk image changes. SEPStorage, nvram.bin, config.plist and
  the identity stay; the guest reads the same bytes, so the SEP/keybag
  pairing is unaffected. Owner, mode and times of Disk.img are kept.
- The walk covers the union of both files' data ranges in 8 MiB
  F_NOCACHE chunks. Differing runs are one pwrite each; where <vm> reads
  as zeros and the base has data the unit is punched, keeping the image
  sparse. A partial unit at EOF is written, never punched.
- The unit is the 16 KiB VM page, not the 4 KiB APFS block: measured on
  macOS 27, a 4 KiB write into a clone replaces the whole page, so
  smaller units would overcount sharing.
- After F_FULLFSYNC the staging file is compared with the original over
  every byte; any difference refuses the swap. Off APFS or across
  volumes the clone fails and nothing is copied. Writing stops while
  less than 4 GiB would stay free. Every failure removes the hidden
  .rebase-<uuid> folder; vm export skips one left by a killed run.
- --dry-run compares in place and prints the same report: logical size,
  bytes shared, written and punched, and the elapsed time.

Savings appear only when nothing else holds the old image's blocks
(snapshots of <vm> or clones made from it keep them); the help text,
create-and-run.md and snapshots.md say so. Research/Host/disk_rebase.md
records the method, the APFS page and hole-filling measurements, and
the live run.

Tests: DiskRebaseTests (13 tests, 64 MiB sparse images, 16/64 KiB and
8 MiB chunks) cover identical, partly different, holes on either side,
shrink and grow, a base ending mid-unit, a partial unit at EOF, sharing
checked block by block with F_LOG2PHYS_EXT, dry-run equals the real
report, refusals (same machine, a held state file on either machine, a
start before the swap, an image changed meanwhile, no free space, a
corrupt staging byte) with nothing left behind, and kept mode and times.
VPhoneCoreKitTests: 415 tests pass; VPhoneCommand Debug builds.

Live: two iPhone99,11 iOS 27.0 (24A435) machines restored separately,
the target's image first copied into blocks of its own. Rebase took
17 s (dry run 5 s): 8.73 GB shared, 11.95 GB written, 0.29 GB punched.
Physical sharing 0.00 -> 8.69 GB, df +8.77 GB, SHA-256 of the 64 GB
image unchanged. A --new-identity clone of the rebased machine booted
under Launchpad and vphoned answered device.info.

subject: Add vphoned service profiles and the first-boot settle wait
message:
Add vphoned service profiles and the first-boot settle wait

A machine template is set up in one boot and every clone inherits it.
Two steps of that boot need vphoned: turning off the launchd jobs a
research VM never uses, and knowing when first-boot work is done so the
template is not changed underneath it.

services.profile / services.profile.apply {profile, groups?, allow?}
(force) disable the trimmed list with the same launchd override as
services.disable, from the next boot. The list for iOS 27 is the 137
jobs measured on svctest-a, plus appstored/itunesstored and the sign-in
follow-up pair; akd, amsaccountsd and appleaccountd only with
groups: ["accounts"]. Other versions have no list and are refused. A
never-disable set (sleepd, CommCenter, cloudd and NanoRegistry, which
make the guest worse when off, plus what vphone's features use) is
refused whatever names it. The labels the profile disabled are recorded
in /var/db/vphoned/service-profile.plist; "none" turns back on only
those, so jobs disabled elsewhere (the OTA block) stay off. Applying
twice changes nothing.

setup.settle waits, read-only, until staged_system_apps is empty, the
app count holds and installd is idle over a few polls, and on timeout
answers settled: false with the signals and unmet conditions. One call
waits at most 110 s, under the host's 120 s read timeout.

device.name.set already pins the name through libdevicename; it now
also returns reboot_required, since CoreDevice and the DHCP lease follow
only after a restart, and device.info carries the pinned and own name.
The name rule moved to GuestDeviceNameRule so it can be tested.

Tests: VPhoneDaemon/Tests/run-logic-tests.sh builds the lists, the
reconciliation and record, the settle verdict and the name rule for the
Mac (285 checks pass). The vphoned scheme builds. Not yet run on a
guest. Docs: Research/Guest/service_trimming.md (lists, traps,
measurements, revert) and the API reference.

subject: Add vphoned system app removal and orig-fs snapshot deletion
message:
Add vphoned system app removal and orig-fs snapshot deletion

apps.remove_system removes Apple's removable apps durably in one call:
for each bundle id it reads the current container from the live app
list, refuses anything outside /private/var/containers/Bundle/Application
/<UUID>/ (Phone and the rest of /Applications), clones the whole
container to /private/var/mobile/Library/removed-system-apps/
<bundle_id>.container with a manifest beside it, unregisters the app and
only then removes the container, so installd has nothing to repair it
from. One respring at the end; results are per app, an absent app is a
no-op and a half-done removal is finished. apps.restore_system moves a
backup back to its UUID path and registers it through
LSApplicationWorkspace, since icli's registerApp refuses Apple's apps;
apps.removed_system lists the backups.

apfs.snapshots lists a volume's snapshots and apfs.snapshot.delete
deletes only the orig-fs.disabled.rn-* snapshot CFW install leaves on
the system volume, which pins every block a file trim frees. Nothing
matched is success, ENOENT counts as deleted, EBUSY is retryable and
EPERM names the entitlement. vphoned gains
com.apple.developer.vfs.snapshot for it.

The path, identifier, manifest, snapshot-name and errno rules and the
fs_snapshot_list batch parser are checked on the Mac by
VPhoneDaemon/Tests/run-system-maintenance-tests.sh.
Research/Guest/template_snapshot_deletion.md records why the snapshot
must go before trimming saves space, the kernel's requirements, the
host's SIP refusal and the measured 1.19 GB reclaim.

subject: Fix vphoned snapshot entitlement and system app backups across volumes
message:
Fix vphoned snapshot entitlement and system app backups across volumes

The first live run of the P1 verbs found two failures in vphoned.

apfs.snapshot.delete always answered not_permitted. On iOS 27 the
kernel refuses fs_snapshot_delete to a root caller that carries only
com.apple.developer.vfs.snapshot: a prototype signed with that one and
platform-application failed with EPERM, while the same prototype with
com.apple.private.vfs.snapshot instead deleted the orig-fs snapshot.
vphoned now carries com.apple.private.vfs.snapshot in place of the
developer entitlement, and the not_permitted message names it.

apps.restore_system always failed with EXDEV. The backups lived in
/private/var/mobile/Library/removed-system-apps, which is on the User
volume, while the bundle containers are on the Data volume, so the
restore's rename(2) could not cross and the backup's clonefile silently
fell back to a full copy. Backups now go to
/private/var/db/vphoned/removed-system-apps, root only (0700) beside
vphoned's other state on the Data volume: the backup is a clone and the
restore is a rename. If a clone fails anyway, the backup is a copy that
keeps owners, modes, extended attributes and flags (copyfile
COPYFILE_ALL | COPYFILE_RECURSIVE | COPYFILE_NOFOLLOW), and
backup_method says which. Backups the first version left in the old
directory are still listed (legacy: true, with legacy_directory and
legacy_other) and restored: on EXDEV the container is copied the same
way to a staging name beside its UUID path, renamed into place, and the
legacy copy removed (restore_method: "copy"). A new removal drops a
legacy backup of the same app.

setup.settle counted icli's app count, one higher than apps.list on the
iOS 27 template; both now count the same list, the records with a
bundle identifier.

Tests: run-system-maintenance-tests.sh checks the directory search
order, legacy detection and the EXDEV rule (131 checks);
run-logic-tests.sh 285 checks; the VPhone bundle builds in Release and
passes bundle admission, with com.apple.private.vfs.snapshot in
vphoned's signature. Docs: the API reference, the snapshot deletion
requirements and the post-setup system app notes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Pass vphoned's whole error object through vphone.sock
message:
Pass vphoned's whole error object through vphone.sock

A refused vphoned call carries more than a message: apps.remove_system
puts per-app results in its command_failed body, apfs.snapshot.delete
adds reason, errno and retryable. The host dropped all of it. The
vphone.sock rpc verb answered {"ok":false,"error":"<message>"}, because
VPhoneGuestControl kept only error.message, so "see results" pointed at
nothing and an automation could not tell a retryable busy from a hard
refusal.

VPhoneGuestControl.call keeps throwing ControlError.guestError with the
message, so every existing caller is unchanged; a new
rpcAfterQueuedInput throws GuestRPCFailure with the error object as
vphoned sent it. The rpc verb uses it and adds that object as
guest_error, keeping error as the message string, so the reply only
gains a field. Launchpad's guest socket appends guest_error, when a
bundle sends it, to the error detail as one line of sorted JSON, which
vphone-launchpad-cli guest rpc prints last on stderr; with an older
bundle it prints what it did before. Nothing Launchpad relies on in the
bundle changes, so the series stays.

The VirtualMachine target has no tests. The VPhone bundle and
VPhoneLaunchpad build in Release; VPhoneLaunchpad/Tests pass.

subject: Add machine templates and template-backed vm create
message:
Add machine templates and template-backed vm create

A template is a complete machine that never boots, kept in
<library>/.templates/<id>/ with a Template.plist. New machines are
cloned from it with a new identity, so a second machine for the same
firmware is a clonefile and a few seconds instead of a restore.

The key (VPhoneMachineTemplateKey, pure, in CoreKit) is the guest
device, the iOS and cloudOS versions and builds, the preset, a digest
of the boot-chain patches it resolves to and its parameters, the
bundle series, the disk size and the slimming done to the guest
(nothing yet: trim tier none, no setup boot). The identifier is the
first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of one line per field; a test pins
one against shasum. vphone-cli resolves the same key from the
requested options and IPSWs before a create, and from a machine's
restore-info.json, PatchPlan.plist, config.plist, disk and
launchpad.json when it is adopted.

- vm template list/show/adopt/delete. list --json marks a template
  stale when the series differs, the preset now resolves to another
  boot-chain digest, or FirmwarePatchDrift finds a boot-chain patch
  whose receipt disagrees with the plan. adopt freezes a stopped
  machine (no snapshots) by one exclusive rename; --force adopts one
  that would be stale.
- vm create defaults to templates: it resolves the key, clones from a
  matching template, or builds one first in
  .templates/.building-<id>-<uuid>/<id>/ under a flock on
  .templates/.lock-<id>, checks the built records give the same key,
  freezes it in one rename and clones the machine from it. The
  template is never booted; the clone gets the first boot check.
  --no-template keeps the old pipeline exactly. --template <id> clones
  from a named template without root or IPSWs and refuses --device,
  --preset or --disk-size that differ. New --cpu, --memory,
  --network, --unlock-at-startup and --skip-first-boot.
- A frozen template never boots: VPhoneLibrary.bundle(named:) now
  takes only a machine name, so no verb reaches .templates; vm launch
  and VPhoneBootCommand.validate (vphone-vm, DFU included) refuse a
  frozen record or a folder directly in .templates. A clone drops
  Template.plist.
- VPhoneMachineTemplates.recordSteps lets the offline trim and the
  setup boot record their work in a template still being built;
  freeze and adopt refuse steps that do not match the key.

Live test on iPhone17,3 27.0 (24A435) / cloudOS 26.4: a Launchpad
machine adopted in 0.4 s; two clones made in 0.06 s each booted side
by side through Launchpad with new UDIDs, vphoned answering, their
CPU and memory applied and lockdown DeviceName p2-a and p2-b. After
two minutes each clone held 1.1 GB of its own on disk, 3.2 GB after
seven (first-boot work the setup boot is meant to absorb). Deleting
the template freed its 0.12 GB of unshared blocks and the clones kept
booting.

Only vm create and new verbs change; Launchpad uses none of them yet,
so the series stays. VPhoneCoreKitTests pass (429); the VPhone bundle
builds in Release and passes bundle admission. The VPhoneCommand
target has no test target, so the creator is covered live only.

subject: Give templates a setup boot and slimming switches
message:
Give templates a setup boot and slimming switches

A template now boots once before it is frozen, so every clone starts at
the Lock Screen with first-boot work done and the guest slimmed, instead
of each clone running Setup and writing its own first-boot state.

The setup boot (VPhoneTemplateSetupBoot, CoreKit) drives vphoned through
vphone.sock in a fixed order, each step with a deadline: delete the
orig-fs snapshot, setup.skip, setup.settle (110 s calls up to 10 min),
apps.remove_system, services.profile.apply with the sign-in follow-up
group checked, reboot (told apart by launchd's start time), verify (no
snapshot, Setup done, no profile service running, removed apps absent,
vphoned answering), clear the device name vphone-vm pinned, and a clean
shutdown. Calls that did not reach vphoned or that guest_error marks
retryable or busy are repeated; setup.skip, which refuses for a while
early in a first boot, is retried on any refusal. A failed step kills the
VM, names the step and records nothing, so the build is never frozen.

- Switches on vm create and vm template setup: --slim on|off,
  --service-profile none|trimmed, --remove-apps on|off, --keep-apps,
  --accounts-off. Defaults: trimmed profile and list C (App Store, Home,
  TV, News, FaceTime, iTunes Store, Messages, Games, Find My, Wallet;
  never Phone or Camera). --slim off still skips Setup and deletes the
  snapshot. Contradictions are refused; --no-template takes none and
  --template <id> checks them against the template.
- The key gains slimming.serviceGroups (--accounts-off); format 2.
- vm create builds the template, runs its setup boot after cfw install
  (where offline trimming records its tier) and freezes it.
- vm template setup <vm> works on a stopped machine, including one
  Launchpad left at Setup after its first boot, and records the steps
  for vm template adopt; given a .building-… name it finishes a failed
  build to its key and freezes it.
- A staging machine's vphone.sock path is about 125 bytes, past
  sun_path. VPhoneUnixSocket binds and connects such a path through a
  link to its folder in a private folder under /tmp.

Live on iPhone17,3 27.0 (24A435): a Launchpad machine's setup boot took
2 min 16 s; two clones booted to the Lock Screen and Home Screen with
Setup done, the ten apps gone, 141 services off, no snapshot and their
own device names. Each clone held 0.58 GB of its own after seven minutes
(3.2 GB from a template without a setup boot). VPhoneCoreKitTests pass
(463, the step machine against a scripted guest); the VPhone bundle
builds in Release and passes bundle admission.

subject: Trim template System volumes offline and keep templates lean
message:
Trim template System volumes offline and keep templates lean

A template build can now delete system files the guest never needs from
its System volume, after cfw install and before the setup boot. The
tiers are a versioned CoreKit table (VPhoneSystemTrim, list version 1):
conservative removes the contents of usr/standalone/update; standard
adds the SharingDeviceAssets pre-installed asset, the watch faces and
the LinguisticData RequiredAssets bundles of languages not kept
(--keep-languages, default en,zh-Hans,zh; English is always kept);
aggressive is reserved and refused until it is validated. The key value
records tier, list version and kept languages (standard/1/en,zh,zh-Hans),
so templates trimmed differently never match.

The trim needs no root. VPhoneMachineTemplateTrimmer attaches Disk.img
without mounting, finds the System volume by its APFS role (diskutil apfs
list -plist, checked against the attached physical store), mounts it
nosuid,nodev,noowners,nobrowse in a mkdtemp folder, and deletes each
entry through VPhoneConfinedDirectory: O_NOFOLLOW walks, links deleted as
links, no volume changes, every target checked against the list first,
and nothing at all unless SystemVersion.plist is there. It logs the
allocated bytes removed per entry (removeItem now returns them), always
unmounts and detaches, and records Steps.TrimTier.

- vm template trim <machine|.building-…> --tier --keep-languages --json,
  for Launchpad to call on a stopped staging machine. It refuses a
  running machine, a frozen template, a clone of a template, and a trim
  that would narrow one already recorded. On a library machine without
  a Template.plist it writes an unfrozen one keyed from its records
  (recordSteps(creating:)), so adopt sees the steps.
- vm create --trim none|conservative|standard and --keep-languages; a
  --template whose trim differs conflicts, --no-template refuses a trim.
- The trimmed blocks stay pinned by the guest's orig-fs snapshot, which
  only the setup boot can delete. A key with a trim but no setup boot is
  refused before anything is built, and freeze and adopt refuse a trim
  whose SnapshotDeleted is false: such a template would cost what an
  untrimmed one does while its clones have lost the files. The default
  trim is therefore standard for a template with a setup boot and none
  until then.
- Templates never keep the restore tree: buildTemplate removes it
  whatever --keep-artifacts says (which now keeps it only with
  --no-template, with a warning otherwise), and freeze and adopt remove
  it too.
- A machine cloned from a template records it in TemplateSource.plist;
  vm clone keeps it, vm export leaves it out. vm template list/show
  print each template's machines and allocated size, vm info and the
  bundle report its template, and vm delete of the last machine using a
  template that still exists prints a note to delete it. Nothing deletes
  a template on its own.

Live on iPhone17,3 27.0 (24A435): a Launchpad-created machine, stopped,
trimmed standard in 4.7 s without root: 361.7 MB, 237.6 MB, 147.9 MB and
418.7 MB, 1.17 GB in all, while Disk.img stayed at 35.98 M blocks (the
snapshot). A second run removed nothing; narrowing to conservative,
aggressive, and adopt --force were refused. The machine booted through
Launchpad to the Setup greeting with vphoned answering and 258 apps.
Two clones of a throwaway template showed under "machines using it",
and deleting the second printed the note.

VPhoneCoreKitTests pass (452). VPhoneCommand builds, and the VPhone
bundle builds in Release and passes bundle admission.

subject: Attach the template trim's disk image with diskutil
message:
Attach the template trim's disk image with diskutil

#630 moved every host disk-image call from the deprecated hdiutil to
diskutil; the offline trim this branch adds still ran `hdiutil attach
-nomount -imagekey diskimage-class=CRawDiskImage` and `hdiutil detach`.

Attach with `diskutil image attach -noMount`, which has no image-class
key and needs none: it attaches the headerless Disk.img as raw and
mounts none of its volumes. Eject with `diskutil eject`, falling back to
a forced `diskutil unmountDisk` and a second eject, the form #630 uses
because macOS 15 accepts it. A failed attach is now read for a device
before its exit status, and that device is ejected.

The attach output is `<device>\t<content>` lines, the image's disk
first and then the synthesized container's `Apple_APFS_Container` and
`Apple_APFS_Volume` lines; the parser already skips those. Its test now
uses that output as captured on macOS 27.0.1, plus the container-first
order hdiutil printed.

Also read the trim's mkdtemp name while its buffer is pinned, the
same fix #631 made for the cfw work folder.

Live, Release vphone-cli on a plain clone of a stopped iOS 27.0 iPhone
machine: standard trim removed 1,165,852,672 bytes, a second run 0, and
no disk image, mount or work folder was left behind.

subject: Find a create's template without its IPSWs, and record where templates came from
message:
Find a create's template without its IPSWs, and record where templates came from

Launchpad needs to know, before it restores anything, whether a template
for New Machine's options exists. Working that out itself would copy the
key logic, whose boot-chain digest needs the patch catalog and the plan
resolver.

`vm template find` resolves the key the way `vm create` does and reports
the template with it, current or stale, without downloading, restoring or
changing the library. The builds come from the IPSWs when they are local
or in the IPSW cache (`VPhoneIPSWCache.localArchive`, which never
downloads), otherwise from a template whose record names the same two
sources, so a request still resolves after its IPSWs were deleted.
`--block` and `--allow` carry per-patch overrides, which have a boot-chain

prints the new template as `vm template show --json` does, with progress

`vm template setup` and `vm template trim` line-buffer stdout, so a

subject: Create Launchpad machines from slimmed templates
message:
Create Launchpad machines from slimmed templates

New Machine now clones a machine from a template by default. Its first
step runs `vm template find`. A current template is cloned at once (`vm
create --template <id> --skip-first-boot` with the CPU, memory and
network asked for) and booted. Otherwise the template is built in a
temporary library machine, `template-` and eight hex digits, by the usual
restore steps and `cfw install` through the helper, then `vm template
trim`, the headless `vm template setup` and `vm template adopt --json`
with the IPSW sources, and the machine is cloned from it. The steps show
under Template and Machine with durations; the setup boot shows its own
stage, and a failed step carries the line vphone-cli ended with. A retry
from Find Template decides again. An adopt that loses to another
creation of the same key uses that template and deletes the build. Once a
creation has built a template, it offers to delete the two IPSWs it came
from, after a confirmation.

The General page has a Slim System switch; a new Template page holds
Create from a template (off restores the machine on its own, with keys of
its own, and explains the shared SEP and Data volume keys), the trim tier
and kept languages, the service profile, Apple Account and the system
apps to remove (Camera and Phone never). Contradictions the CLI refuses
are not offered. `vphone-launchpad-cli vm create` takes the same switches
and `--no-template`.

File > Templates… lists every library's templates (device, OS, preset,
slimming, size, machines, current or outdated with the reasons, created)
and deletes them and unfinished builds, saying that clones keep working
and what deleting frees now. Guest System… switches a running machine's
service profile (`services.profile.apply`, with a Restart Guest offer)
and restores removed system apps (`apps.removed_system`,
`apps.restore_system`); a stopped machine gets an explanation. The
inspector and the machine list show each machine's exclusive disk use
(ATTR_CMNEXT_PRIVATESIZE, measured off the main actor at most every 30 s)
beside what its files allocate, and the template it came from. Deleting
the last machine of a template shows the note `vm delete` prints.

No new root path: `cfw install` runs on the temporary machine, a visible
library machine, before it is adopted; trim, setup and adopt run as the
user. The setup boot's vphone-vm is started by vphone-cli, a pipe child
of Launchpad like the DFU boot, not through the launcher, so Launchpad is
its responsible process while it runs, and the quit confirmation for a
running creation covers it.

Launchpad now runs vphone-cli verbs and options 2.8 does not have. The
unreleased 2.9 series already requires a 2.9.0 bundle, so the minimum
stays and its comment lists them.

Tests: TemplatesTests.sh is new (switch mapping, argument construction
for find, trim, setup, adopt and clone, the step plan, list and find JSON
decoding, the delete note, private sizes of a real clonefile and their
formatting); every Launchpad test script passes. Debug Launchpad builds
without warnings; the Release VPhone bundle passes admission. The new
strings are in all five languages. Screens checked in the DEBUG snapshot
mode under com.vphone.launchpad.repro, light and dark, in English and
Simplified Chinese; nothing ran against a real machine.

subject: Keep templates under the key their request asked for, and find them without downloading
message:
Keep templates under the key their request asked for, and find them without downloading

The Launchpad 2.9 end-to-end test (PR #633) found four CLI problems.

B1. Once in two setup boots on 27.0, `apps.remove_system` left Find My
registered: IcliKit's `unregisterApp` looks at LaunchServices right after
`icli_unregister_app` and reported "still lists the app after
unregistration". `vm template setup` on a machine only warned, the steps
recorded nine apps, and `adopt` saved the template under a key `vm
template find` never computes for the default options, so every later
create missed it and built another 17.5 GB template.

- vphoned polls the record every 0.1 s for up to 2.5 s after
  unregistering, unregisters once more if the app is still listed, waits
  again, and only then fails the app (`GuestAppUnregistration`, the
  decision as pure logic). `unregister_attempts` in an app's result says
  when the retry was needed.
- `vm template setup <vm> --strict` fails the setup boot, recording
  nothing, on an app not removed, and checks after the service profile
  that nothing else fell short of the plan
  (`VPhoneTemplateSetupOutcome.deviations(from:)`). A template build in
  `vm create` and a `.building-…` setup were already strict.
- `vm template adopt <vm> --expect <id>` refuses before anything moves
  unless the machine's records give template `<id>`. It recovers the key
  behind `<id>` from the library's templates and builds, or among the
  keys that differ only in slimming (any subset of the default apps,
  profile, groups, trim tier, setup boot; about 25,000 hashes, 50 ms), and
  names each differing field ("removed apps: expected com.apple.findmy
  removed too, the machine still has it"); otherwise it spells out the
  machine's canonical description. With `--json` the refusal also goes
  to stdout: adopted false, error unexpected_template, message, id,
  expected, key, expectedKey, differences, canonicalDescription, steps;
  exit status 1.

B3. `vm create` resolved its sources with `resolveSources` first and
downloaded both IPSWs (13 GB) before looking for a template. It now
resolves the builds as `vm template find` does
(`VPhoneMachineTemplates.resolveBuilds`: local or cached IPSWs, else the
newest template recorded with the same sources) and downloads only when
no template matches and it has to build one.

B4. `VPhoneIPSWCache.localArchive` answers nil for a local path that no
longer exists, so `find` (and `create`) fall back to a template's
recorded sources instead of failing "IPSW not found". A file that is
there but not an IPSW still fails.

B8. `vm template delete` says that machines cloned from the template
still share its blocks only when the usage scan finds such machines, and
otherwise that its space is free now (`deletionNote`).

machine_templates.md, create-and-run.md and vphoned_http_api.md describe
the new behavior and flags. Launchpad itself is not changed here.

Tests: VPhoneCoreKitTests 501 pass (new: build resolution order with a
fake local reader, the --expect mismatch for a left-behind app, other
slimming, a known and an unknown key, strict deviations and the strict
machine run, the delete note); VPhoneArchiveKitTests 71 pass (a missing
local IPSW is nil, a junk one still throws); vphoned's
run-system-maintenance-tests (148, the poll and retry decision and its
loop), run-logic-tests and run-hierarchy-tests pass. Against a scratch
library with a hand-made machine (no guest): find with deleted local
IPSWs reports unresolved instead of failing; adopt --expect refuses with
the Find My difference and the JSON object, adopts with the right id;
delete prints the right note with and without a clone. The setup boot
itself was not run against a guest.

subject: Measure exclusive disk use by physical extents, not APFS private size
message:
Measure exclusive disk use by physical extents, not APFS private size

The Exclusive size of machines and templates came from APFS's private
size (ATTR_CMNEXT_PRIVATESIZE). A Time Machine local snapshot shares
every block that existed when it was taken, so after each hourly
snapshot every machine and template showed 0 bytes until it wrote again,
and deleting one looked like it freed nothing (B7 in the 2.9 end-to-end
test).

Launchpad now maps each file's data ranges with SEEK_DATA/SEEK_HOLE and
F_LOG2PHYS_EXT and measures every machine and template folder of every
library in one pass: a stretch of the device covered by exactly one
folder is that folder's own. Snapshots are not among the files compared,
so what they pin counts as the folder's own, which deleting it frees once
they expire; the help texts say so. A booted 64 GB sparse image (21.6 GB,
123,030 ranges) maps in about 0.1 s and the sweep over three takes 3 ms.
Ranges are kept per file and mapped again only when its size, mtime or
ctime changes, with a 15 s budget per pass.

Mapping opens the image, and lsof then lists Launchpad for it, which
vm stop and cfw install read as the machine running. Launchpad never
opens a folder it is creating, exporting or installing into, uses the
last ranges for those, and leaves its own process out of its lsof check.
Templates are measured with the machines instead of separately.

subject: Keep template builds on the key Find computed; guest overrides go to the clone
message:
Keep template builds on the key Find computed; guest overrides go to the clone

Three faults the Launchpad 2.9 template test found in New Machine's
pipeline.

A setup boot that could not remove an app (LaunchServices still listed
Find My) left it out of the recorded key, and the adopt saved the build
under another id than `vm template find` had computed. The creation
succeeded, but every later one with the same options found nothing and
built a 17 GB template again. The setup step now passes `--strict`, which
fails it when an app stays, and the adopt passes `--expect <id>` with the
id Find Template computed (or, when Find could not resolve the key before
the IPSWs were downloaded, the id a second find gives after the restore).
A build whose key differs fails Save template with the fields the CLI
names, instead of being saved under an id no later creation finds. Both
options come with the matching vphone-cli change of the same series.

Per-patch overrides were handled as one set. A template that matched was
cloned and booted without them, so a guest patch blocked or allowed in
Patch Settings was silently dropped; and a template that had to be built
got all of them through `fw set-patches`, so the guest ones were written
into the template and passed on to later creates that never asked for
them. The overrides are now split where the template key splits them,
by the bundle's own catalog (`fw patches --json`): a patch on a boot-chain
component, any `.firmware` target including Filesystem and Manifest, or
one the catalog does not list, counts as boot chain. Find Template and the
build get the boot-chain overrides only. When guest overrides exist, a new
Apply guest patches step follows the clone: `fw set-patches` with every
override on the new machine, then `cfw update-environment` through the
helper's existing verb, before its first boot. No new root path. Without
a template nothing changes: `cfw install` applies every override to the
machine itself. The Advanced page says so when guest patches differ.

The create report of `vphone-launchpad-cli vm create` named the temporary
build machine even when a template was found and nothing was built. It now
gives `buildMachine` only once Find Template has decided to build; the key
stays, as null otherwise.

Tests: TemplatesTests covers `--strict`, `--expect` with and without an
id, the boot-chain and guest split and the `fw set-patches` and find
arguments it gives, the Apply guest patches step in both plans, and the
build name the report gives; every Launchpad test script passes. New
strings in en, ja, ko, vi and zh-Hans. The snapshot driver shows the
Advanced page with guest overrides and the creation sheet applying them.

subject: Keep Guest System's restart note until the guest restarts
message:
Keep Guest System's restart note until the guest restarts

Switching the service profile to None turns back on what the profile

clears its record at once, and `reboot_required` is counted from the

with the guest boot it was made in (launchd's start time, from
`processes.list`). The note and the button show while it is kept, also
when the sheet is opened again. It is forgotten once the guest answers
from a later boot, when the machine stops, or when an apply needs no
restart. Restart Guest waits up to three minutes for the guest to come
back from a new boot and reads the sheet again. No vphoned change: both
RPCs exist.

VPhoneLaunchpadServiceProfile moves to VPhoneLaunchpadTemplates.swift
beside the new VPhoneLaunchpadPendingRestart so TemplatesTests can reach
both; the tests cover reading launchd's start time, the apply's answer
being kept over the profile's, a second change keeping the first boot,
and what counts as a later boot. The snapshot driver shows the sheet

subject: Signal only a machine's own processes in vm stop
message:
Signal only a machine's own processes in vm stop

`vm stop` sent SIGINT to every process `lsof` listed for the machine's
Disk.img when it found no vphone-vm, and SIGKILL to every holder left
after its timeout. Anything that merely had the image open could be
killed: Launchpad maps a running machine's extents for about 0.1 s every
30 s, and Spotlight, a backup tool or our own trim and rebase open it
too. The PR #633 retest saw Launchpad in that window (N2).

Holders are now classified by executable (`proc_pidpath`,
VPhoneProcessHolder). Only vphone-vm, from any bundle copy, and
Virtualization's com.apple.Virtualization.VirtualMachine service run a
machine; a service holding this machine's disk belongs to it. `vm stop`
asks the vphone-vm of the machine's config, or without one the VM
processes holding its disk, and after the timeout SIGKILLs only VM
processes still holding the disk or the vphone-vm of that config, found
again so a reused PID is not hit. Other holders are named and left
alone; a machine held only by them is reported as not running.

`cfw install`, `update-environment` and `update-kernel`, and
VPhoneBundleActivity.requireStopped (clone, snapshot, revert, adopt,
trim, setup boot), still refuse any other holder, since a file another
process has open is not standing still, but their refusals now name
each holder's executable and say when none of them runs the VM.
VPhoneBundleActivityError.running carries the holders; a
`running(name:pids:)` convenience looks the executables up.

Tests cover the classification, the PID-order split, both refusal
wordings and the error description. Checked by hand against a fake
vphone-vm and a bystander holding a scratch Disk.img: the fake was
stopped, the bystander kept running.

subject: Count template users by build, and say what a delete frees
message:
Count template users by build, and say what a delete frees

Three findings from the PR #633 retest.

N1: a template deleted and built again with the same key gets the same
identifier, and clones only recorded the identifier, so the clones of
the old build counted as users of the new one: in `vm template
list/show`, Launchpad's "N machine(s) use it" (from find's report) and
the delete notes, although they share none of its blocks. Freezing or
adopting a template now gives it a UUID (`Build` in Template.plist),
and each clone's TemplateSource.plist records it.
VPhoneMachineTemplateSource.isClone(of:) matches the builds, or, when
either record predates them, requires `Cloned` no earlier than the
template's `FrozenAt` (else `Created`). `usage` counts a machine only
for the template it came from, and `vm delete` of an old build's clone
no longer says the new template is unused. The list/show JSON adds
`build` and `frozenAt`; `show` prints them.

B8: `vm template delete` said "no machine was cloned from it, so its
space is free now" whenever no machine used it, although its clones may
have been deleted before and a local Time Machine snapshot can keep its
blocks. It now says only what it knows: "no machine uses it now;
deleting frees its blocks (a local Time Machine snapshot may keep them
until it expires)", or the machines that use it and that the blocks
they share stay allocated until they change them or are deleted.
`--json` (with `--force`) prints `deleted`, `path`, `machines`,
`blocksFreed` and the same note.

G1: vphoned's per-app `unregister_attempts` never left the setup boot.
VPhoneTemplateSetupAppResult keeps it; the remove-apps step logs
"<bundle id>: unregistered after N attempts", the report adds a summary
line, and Steps records `UnregisterAttempts` (not part of the key), shown
by `vm template show`.

Tests: build match and mismatch, the date fallback for legacy records on
either side, a rebuilt template not counting the old clones (usage and
the `vm delete` note), legacy clone records left out by date, old
records decoding without `Build`, the delete note wording, and the
retried apps in the log, outcome and steps.

subject: Never open the disk of a running machine to measure it
message:
Never open the disk of a running machine to measure it

The retest of PR #633 (N2) found Launchpad's disk meter mapping the
Disk.img of running machines, the user's included: their images change
all the time, so each pass about every 30 s opened them (O_EVTONLY, about
0.1 s). While a file is open, lsof lists Launchpad for it. `vm stop`
SIGINTs every holder when it finds no vphone-vm and SIGKILLs every holder
left at its timeout, so a forced stop could kill Launchpad; `cfw install`
and `update-environment` refuse a disk anyone else holds. The meter only
left out folders in the `.busy` state.

The meter now opens a machine's files only when VPhoneLaunchpadDiskAccess
allows it: no `vm launch` of Launchpad's for it is still running
(starting, running, stopping), the last lsof named no other process for
its disk, and Launchpad has no operation on it (a creation or the
template build in it, an export, queued or running, an install or
update, a shutdown or stop) or on a whole library (an import, a template
deletion). The library asks again right before each file is mapped, so a
machine started during a pass is not opened. Any other machine keeps the
extents mapped last, and a stopped one is opened only when a file's size,
mtime or ctime changed since then. The per-file decision is a pure
function, VPhoneLaunchpadDiskMeter.use, and the 15 s per-pass budget is
unchanged.

Tests: TemplatesTests covers the access rule, every case of the per-file
decision, and on real APFS clones that an unchanged pass asks nothing,
that only a changed folder is asked, that a refusal keeps the last
extents and that the next allowed pass maps the change.
Research/Host/machine_templates.md describes the rule.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Take per-patch overrides in vphone-launchpad-cli vm create
message:
Take per-patch overrides in vphone-launchpad-cli vm create

`vphone-launchpad-cli vm create` took only --preset, so the retest of
PR #633 (B2) could drive Launchpad's Apply guest patches step only by
hand (`exec vm create --template`, `exec fw set-patches`, `cfw
update-environment`). It now takes --block <patch> and --allow <patch>,
each repeatable, with the meaning of New Machine's patch list and
`vphone-cli fw set-patches`.

The control request carries repeatable options in a new optional
`repeated` map, so a request without it still decodes, and the command
table marks them (`[--block <value>]...` in the usage). The CLI's argument
parser moved from main.swift into VPhoneLaunchpadControl.swift as
VPhoneLaunchpadControlRequest.parse, which throws a usage error instead of
exiting, so it can be tested.

Launchpad reads the creation bundle's catalog for the preset (`fw
patches --preset … --json`), refuses an identifier no set declares or one
both blocked and allowed, and keeps only what differs from the preset,
noting the rest, as `fw set-patches` does
(VPhoneLaunchpadPatchOverrides.requested). It warns about boot-essential
patches turned off. The selection and its guest part then go into the
pipeline's options as New Machine passes them: boot-chain overrides into
Find Template and the template build, guest overrides onto the clone in
Apply guest patches. The create report gains a `patches` object. --from
refuses --block and --allow, since a retry keeps the creation's patches.
Launchpad and the bundle are both in the unreleased 2.9 series, so the
series stays.

Tests: the new ControlTests covers parsing, repeated options, their
usage, and decoding a request with and without them; TemplatesTests
covers the reduction, the split, the retest's guest-only case and both
refusals. Documents/Guides/launchpad-cli.md describes the options.

subject: Count only VM processes holding a disk as a running machine in Launchpad
message:
Count only VM processes holding a disk as a running machine in Launchpad

Launchpad took any process holding a machine's Disk.img, other than
itself, for the machine running. With `tail -f nt-a/Disk.img` open,
`vphone-launchpad-cli vm start nt-a` failed with "nt-a is already
running or busy", the window showed the machine as running, and a stop
waited on the guest that was not there (PR #633 retest, L1).

Launchpad now classifies each holder by its executable the way the CLI's
VPhoneProcessHolder does: only vphone-vm (any copy) and Virtualization's
VM service inside Virtualization.framework run a machine. Launchpad does
not link VPhoneCoreKit and must not reference its sources, so the rule
lives in a small VPhoneLaunchpadDiskHolder, which also parses `lsof -F
pn` and names holders as `12925 tail`.

Other holders leave the machine stopped but still held: the disk meter
keeps skipping the image (VPhoneLaunchpadDiskAccess.isHeld, the N2 fix),
and cfw install, update-environment and update-kernel are refused by
name before the helper runs them, in the window and in the Launchpad
CLI, rather than failing inside the helper with "check the log".
`vm list` reports them as `diskOpenIn`.

vm start proceeds with a foreign holder. `vphone-cli vm launch` does not
look at holders at all; Virtualization opens the disk itself and the
start fails in the console log if it cannot. Refusing in Launchpad would
make it stricter than the command it drives, so the Launchpad CLI prints
a note naming the holder instead. A start of a machine that is running
or busy now says which.

subject: Check the disk before rebinding a machine in Launchpad's set-bundle
message:
Check the disk before rebinding a machine in Launchpad's set-bundle

`vphone-launchpad-cli vm set-bundle <vm> <version> --update-environment`
on a stopped machine whose Disk.img another process held (`tail -f`)
wrote the new binding first and only then had the guest environment
update refuse the held disk. The machine ended up rebound with its old
guest environment, and the error did not say the binding had changed.
Change Core Bundle in the window had the same order.

The library's setBundle now goes through VPhoneLaunchpadBundleChange,
which asks for the disk's other holders before anything is written when
the environment is to be updated, then binds, then updates. A held disk
refuses the change for that machine with the binding untouched, naming
the process as the other disk refusals do. Both the control command and
the window get this, since both call setBundle.

An update that fails once it has started keeps the new binding: undoing
it would not undo what the helper already copied into the guest, and
`guestEnvironment` in launchpad.json still names the last bundle whose
environment was installed, which `vm list` and the inspector show. The
error now says so first ("<vm> now runs with Core Bundle <version>, but
its guest environment was not updated"), above the update's own cause,
so the outcome is not mistaken for a refused change.

TemplatesTests holds the order: a held disk refuses before binding, a
failed update keeps the binding, an unwritable binding stops before the
update, and a rebinding without an update does not ask about the disk.

subject: Report only newly shared blocks as a rebase's saving
message:
Report only newly shared blocks as a rebase's saving

vm rebase counted every byte-identical unit as shared, without looking at
whether the two images already stored it in the same blocks. Two machines
cloned from one template are byte-identical over most of their images
because they are the same blocks, so a dry run of one onto the other
reported "shared 17.26 GB" while the target held only about 0.35 GB of its
own and a real rebase would have freed nothing (PR #633 live test, R1).

plan and rebase now map both images with F_LOG2PHYS_EXT, one call per
contiguous extent, and intersect the maps. Identical units split into newly
shared (target data not yet the base's: the saving, now the headline) and
already shared (the base's blocks already, or a hole in the target). The
map comes from the original images, so a dry run and the rebase still
agree; the rebuild and its full verification are unchanged. Below 0.1 GB
newly shared the command says the rebase would free almost nothing.

--onto also takes a template identifier or unique prefix; a machine with
that name wins. A template is never booted, so it is the best base. The
rebase only reads it, and the rebased machine gets no TemplateSource.plist,
so template usage does not count it. When the records show both sides come
from one template build, the command notes it before comparing.

subject: Fix two vm rebase messages
message:
Fix two vm rebase messages

The same-template note said "fz-b was cloned from template … and already
share its blocks" when the base is the template itself; the verb now
follows the subject. A template prefix shorter than four hex digits was
reported only as "No VM or template named …"; the message now says a

subject: Skip Setup Assistant without restarting SpringBoard during data migration
message:
Skip Setup Assistant without restarting SpringBoard during data migration

On a guest's first boot after a restore, DataMigrator runs its plugins
for 60-180 s (the last, SpringBoard.migrator, waits for PosterBoard's
poster migration). Until FrontBoard reaches its DataMigrationCompleted
milestone, SpringBoard has not decided whether to run Setup and
FrontBoard drops the SBSRelaunchAction icli's respring() sends. The
launchctl stop fallback then fails with launchd status 144 ("Requestor
lacks required entitlement"), so setup.skip was refused until migration
ended: 45-98 s of every template setup boot on a fast Mac, and past the
host's 120 s deadline on a MacBook Air, where 2.9.0 could not create a
machine. The 144 comes from the fallback; no entitlement changes when
FrontBoard takes the relaunch.

Keys written before the milestone are read when SpringBoard decides
(the guest went to the Lock Screen with no respring). So setup.skip now
writes the keys and leaves SpringBoard alone while migration runs:
com.apple.migration (mobile) has no LastSystemVersion or
DMLastMigrationResults.buildVersion for kern.osversion and DataMigrator's
XPC service is running. It answers respring {restarted: false, reason:
data_migration_pending}. A restart that still fails after migration is
refused as retryable, with the keys written.

setup.status reports data_migration_done, and setup.settle also waits
until the latest poll does not see migration running, so a template is
never slimmed or frozen before migration ends. That was only a side
effect of the skip's retries before: staged_system_apps empties 26-67 s
earlier.

subject: Stop Launchpad copying the template match and pin its holder rule copy
message:
Stop Launchpad copying the template match and pin its holder rule copy

PR #633 left two VPhoneCoreKit rules written again in Launchpad: which
disk holder runs a machine (VPhoneProcessHolder.kind, copied as
VPhoneLaunchpadDiskHolder.runsMachine) and whether a clone came from the
template that has its identifier now (VPhoneMachineTemplateSource.isClone,
copied with readers of TemplateSource.plist and Template.plist as
VPhoneLaunchpadTemplateOrigin).

Launchpad does not link VPhoneCoreKit on purpose. It ships apart from
VPhone.bundle, works with every bundle of its series and drives each
machine through the vphone-cli of the bundle it is bound to, while the
kit is that bundle's implementation and changes with every build.
Linking it, or a slice of it through a project reference to
VPhoneKit.xcodeproj, would compile Launchpad's build-time copy in place of
the answer of the bundle it talks to and pull the kit's package graph into
Launchpad's build: the copy moves into the linker instead of going away.

Template match: asked of the CLI. Launchpad already runs `vm list --json`
every 5 s per library, and that already read TemplateSource.plist for
`template`. The report now adds `templateMatch` (current, earlierBuild or
deleted, VPhoneMachineTemplates.match), Launchpad decodes it into the
inspector's Template row and no longer reads either plist. The copy had
already drifted: it accepted a template the CLI calls damaged (key not
matching its folder, folder not loading as a machine). A bundle that does
not report the field, or a value Launchpad does not know, leaves the row
out. 2.9 is not released, so the field joins the 2.9 series contract
(noted above minimumBundleComponents) without a version bump.

Disk holder kind: one table, two copies. Launchpad runs lsof itself on
every refresh, every second while waiting for a machine it did not start
to stop, and before operations that need the disk, leaving its own meter
out by PID. Moving that into vphone-cli would add a process and a
library-wide lsof to every `vm list` for a path test that is a host fact,
not bundle data. Both copies are now tested against
VPhoneCoreKitTests/VirtualMachine/ProcessHolderKinds.json
(LaunchLayoutTests and Launchpad's TemplatesTests.sh), so a change to one
copy or to the table fails a test until all agree.

Research/Host/machine_templates.md records the reasoning and lists the
other places Launchpad still reads bundle files or repeats CLI values.
No user-facing string, control protocol or UI change.

subject: Let a clone wait out a reader instead of failing on Launchpad's meter
message:
Let a clone wait out a reader instead of failing on Launchpad's meter

Launchpad 2.9.0's New Machine failed at its clone step right after saving a
template: "VM '<id>' is in use: ... open in process <pid> vphone-launchpad".
The adopt step refreshes the machine list, which starts a disk meter pass.
The meter sees the new .templates/<id> folder, has never mapped it, and
opens its Disk.img (O_EVTONLY, F_LOG2PHYS_EXT, ~0.1 s) because templates
were opened whenever no library-wide operation ran. vm create --template
checks the source with VPhoneBundleActivity.requireStopped, which refuses
any holder, so a clone that started during that mapping failed. Running the
step again passed at once.

CLI: a clone only reads its source, so both of its checks now use
requireStopped(_:waitingForReaders:) with a 2 s wait: while every holder is
a process that runs no machine and the control socket is not live, it asks
again every 0.1 s, then refuses with the same error. A vphone-vm or
Virtualization service holder, or a live socket, refuses at once, so a
clone still cannot take a machine that runs or starts (templates are never
booted). requireStopped itself is unchanged for the writers: cfw install,
snapshot, revert, adopt, trim, rebase and the setup boot stay strict.

Launchpad: the meter leaves every template unopened while a creation of its
own is at its adopt or clone step (VPhoneLaunchpadDiskAccess.templatesMayOpen,
also asked before each file is mapped). The CLI wait covers a mapping already
under way when the step starts, and readers other than Launchpad.

subject: Clear the crash reports a template's own boots left before freezing it
message:

reboots into the installed system before cfw install has copied the OS
cryptex onto the System volume, so launchd finds no dyld cache and the
