boot session UUID, every panic-full seen in setup boots and clones is the
restore's post-restore boot; the console of installed guests showed no panic
in 78 boots (trimmed build, clone, --no-template machine).

each one under /Logs/CrashReporter/ with the existing files.remove, and says

subject: Turn ProMotion on in the standard preset
message:
Turn ProMotion on in the standard preset

The 120 Hz timing element for the paravirtual display leaves standard's
block list and FirmwarePatchSetCatalog.manualOnlyPatches, so a new VM's
guest renders at 120 Hz. The host scans out every frame the guest
presents, the userland follows the advertised rate, and a static screen
costs what it did at 60 Hz. The cost while animating is up to twice the
host CPU and GPU; a VM that blocks the patch keeps 60 Hz. The no-plan
fallback in buildComponentList is on too, so it agrees with standard.
The patcher's own default stays false, so the kernel CFW reference
comparison is unchanged.

The editor now titles it ProMotion, and the naming rule gives cfw to a
patch standard turns on, so kernel-exp-display_refresh_120hz is renamed
kernel-cfw-display_promotion (Swift: proMotionPatch, applyProMotion).
The old identifier shipped from 2.4.2, so a VM may have it checked.
FirmwarePatchSetCatalog.renamedPatches maps it, and
VPhonePatchPresetStore reads PatchSelection, PatchPlan and PatchReceipt
through that map: such a VM resolves instead of failing fw patch with
unknownPatch, and a kernelcache patched under the old name is not drift.

Checked live on a dedicated iPhone17,3 26.6.2 VM built from this change.
The standard plan enabled the patch, its record landed at 0xEB1A98, and
a legacy selection naming the old identifier read as applied with
nothing pending. With the 2.9.0 guest components SpringBoard deadlocked
on every 120 Hz boot: a guest spindump shows its main thread holding
libvphoneattitude's lock in the setDeviceMotionUpdateInterval: hook while
waiting for Core Motion's MotionThread, which waits for that lock in the
isDeviceMotionActive hook. That is the lock-order bug
Lakr233/vphone-cli#643 fixes. With its fix cherry-picked the same guest
booted at 120 Hz and scrolled Settings at 119.3 frames per second (98.5%
of gaps under 12.5 ms). This needs to ship with #643.

Tests pin standard turning ProMotion on for every base, blocking it per
VM, the no-plan fallback, and the rename map. Research notes are in
Research/Guest/display_refresh_rate.md and

subject: Keep the guest's clock on the Mac's
message:
Keep the guest's clock on the Mac's

A guest was found 18 h 28 min behind the Mac, with the right time zone. A
guest boots with the Mac's time, from the virtual RTC, but once timed has set
the clock from a time source it finds its saved state invalid on every later
boot, starts its filter from the modification time of
/var/db/timed/com.apple.timed.plist, the last time the guest ran, and moves
the clock there. Only an NTP result corrects that, so a guest whose NTP does
not get through, such as one behind a proxy on the Mac that does not carry
UDP 123, is left behind by as long as it was powered off. A Mac that sleeps
leaves a running guest behind as well.

vphoned gains `time.clock` (REST `GET/PUT /v1/clock`, capability `clock`).
Read alone, it returns the guest's clock and whether timed sets it. `{time}`
is the Mac's time: a guest within a second of it is left alone, and so is
one with automatic time off, whose clock was set by hand in Settings.
Otherwise the time is offered to timed with CoreTime's `TMSetSourceTime` as
an NTP result, and timed sets the clock and posts the change itself. timed
turns down a result its filter does not expect until it has seen five from a
source it counts, which NTP is, so the offer is repeated up to six times; an
uncertainty of 0.1 s keeps an offer over a second out from being averaged in.
`{automatic}` turns automatic time on or off. timed takes a source's time
only from a client with the source in `com.apple.timed.sources`, so vphoned's
entitlements gain that with `NTP`.

vphone-vm sends the Mac's time after every connect, every minute, when the
Mac wakes and when the Mac's own clock is set (`VPhoneClockSync`).

Tested on new iPhone17,3 guests on iOS 26.6.2 (23G90) and iOS 27.0.1
(24A446): booted after some minutes off, they came up 302 to 406 s behind
and were on the Mac's time at connect; offers 1.5 s and an hour ahead and a
day behind moved the clock to within 5 ms; 0.5 s ahead and a guest with
automatic time off were left alone; a guest left ahead was back within a
minute. On 26.6.2 a date picked in Settings was kept, and Set Automatically
brought the Mac's time back. Not run: a Mac that sleeps and wakes, and a
change of the Mac's own clock. The analysis, the limits and the results are
in Research/Guest/host_clock_sync.md.

subject: Re-attest the dyld cache header page after clamping maxSlide
message:
Re-attest the dyld cache header page after clamping maxSlide

dyld-boot-maxslide zeroed maxSlide in the main chunk's header and left
page 0's code slot alone. The kernel does not check that page, so the
guest boots, but Xcode's dsc_extractor does: `xcodebuild
-prepareDeviceSupport` stops on "dyld shared cache code signature for
page 0 is incorrect" and still marks the copy done. Device Support then
holds only the DriverKit cache, LLDB reads every system library from
guest memory, and an app launched under the debugger (any Flutter debug
run on iOS 26+) sits on a black screen for about two minutes.

The patcher now re-attests page 0 after the write, and repairs the slot
on a header already at maxSlide 0 without writing the field. cfw install
and update-environment re-run this verb whenever it is live, because its
undo record does not tell the old implementation from the new, so an
existing guest is repaired by its next environment update.
